content.question: How are sentences or documents represented when applying CNNs to NLP?
options: As matrices, where each row corresponds to a token represented as a dense vector (embedding), and filters capture local patterns like n-grams.
As graphs, where each node is a sentence and edges are grammar rules.
As audio spectrograms of the spoken sentences.
As one-hot vectors of the whole vocabulary for the entire document at once.
content.answer: As matrices, where each row corresponds to a token represented as a dense vector (embedding), and filters capture local patterns like n-grams.
